Team,

I pulled the scorecards for Ethan Owens (onsite yesterday) and we have a pretty wide spread across reviewers: 2x 4/5, 1x 2/5, 1x 3/5. We need to reconcile before the hiring sync tomorrow so we can provide a clear recommendation to Hiring.

Can each reviewer reply with a 1-2 sentence rationale for their score and flag any "must-raise" behavioral or technical concerns? If you can, attach the snippet from your notes that influenced the score.

Attached: scorecard_ethan_owens.pdf (my consolidated export) and the onsite invite for context.

Goal: get a short summary from everyone by EOD today PST so I can stitch a recommendation and, if necessary, propose a quick calibration call.

Thanks —

Ava — thanks for pulling this. Quick rationale from me:

- Score: 4/5
- Key reasons: strong systems design thinking, clear understanding of trade-offs around latency vs cost, asked follow-up clarifying questions when we discussed concurrency.
- Notes excerpt: "Good decomposition of requirements; called out edge cases around KV cache invalidation and offered two mitigation strategies (cache segmentation + short TTL)."
- Concerns: occasionally vague on implementation specifics (didn’t name libraries he’d use), but nothing blocking.

Happy to talk live if we want to probe the implementation gap further.

—Marissa

Ava / all — my short take:

- Score: 2/5
- Key reasons: candidate struggled with the distributed debugging exercise. Could not clearly identify where the request fanout was causing the memory spike and proposed a broad retry/backoff approach that would mask symptoms rather than diagnose root cause.
- Notes excerpt: "Suggested increasing batch size (unsafe given tail latency) and implementing global locks — missed the partitioning signal)."
- Concern level: moderate — not a dealbreaker on its own, but given the role's need to own production incidents, this gap matters.

I'm open to a follow-up technical question set to validate whether this was an interview cold-start issue vs. a real gap.

-David

All — I appreciate the quick notes. Proposing a pragmatic path to consensus before the Hiring sync:

Option A (fast): average the technical scores but apply a "production-incident" veto — if any reviewer flags a serious on-call/incident concern (David did), escalate to a 15-minute calibration call.

Option B (definitive): David sends 3 targeted follow-up questions (30–45 min). Candidate responds to the set; we judge pass/fail. This preserves fairness but takes longer (candidate availability dependent).

I recommend Option A for speed unless David strongly prefers B. If we do A, we should add 1 concrete mitigation: ask candidate clarifying follow-ups in the offer conversation (if we get there) and include a short shadow-on-call trial as a condition for leveling.

Proposed immediate steps:
- David: confirm whether you want a follow-up question set (yes/no) by EOD.
- Marissa/Tessa: if you can, add one-sentence strengths summary to the Drive doc by 6pm PT.
- Ava: if no objections, I'll average and flag David's veto to Hiring.

Laura
